description: Building "The Earth Information Jukebox" for NASA Space Apps — turning Earth science visuals (air quality, temperature, climate data) into sound, making it accessible to everyone, including people who can't see the visuals. Looking for teammates with web dev (JS/HTML), audio programming (Web Audio API/Tone.js), or UI/UX skills. If you love climate tech or creative audio-visual tools, join us!
summary:
Planet FM is an interactive web experience that turns NASA Earth Information Center data into music, so people can listen to the state of their planet instead of decoding complex maps and datasets. Users search for their location, such as Dhaka, and choose from topics including air quality, greenhouse gases, wildfires, sea level rise, water resources, agriculture, energy, biodiversity and disasters. The app plays “tracks” for indicators within each topic, such as AQI and PM2.5 for air quality, turning changes in the data into sound alongside a matching visual graph. A calendar lets users replay how conditions have changed over time, and community features let them contribute photos and local information and join environmental campaigns.

The challenge asks for new ways to make Earth science data understandable and engaging. Planet FM makes environmental information personal, local and emotional, and accessible to people who can’t easily read charts or maps. It helps students, communities and individuals see, and hear, how a changing planet affects their surroundings.
details:
Planet FM turns NASA Earth Information Center data into an interactive “radio” for our planet. Users search for their location, choose a topic such as air quality, greenhouse gases, wildfires, sea level rise, water resources or agriculture, and press play on “tracks” for each indicator (for example AQI and PM2.5). The data is turned into sound and shown with a matching graph, and a vinyl-style calendar lets users listen to how conditions changed over time. Community features let people share photos and local information and join environmental campaigns.

Complex datasets and maps are hard for most people to understand, so we made environmental information personal, engaging and accessible, even for people who struggle with visual charts. Our goal is to help students and communities understand how changes in the environment affect their surroundings and encourage them to act. We built it using Figma with NASA data. The creativity comes from the music metaphor: playlists, tracks and records make serious climate data feel familiar and memorable.
